answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bond locked before an account may vote or claim rewards. The protocol caps each bond’s weight and slashes it when independently checked interactions reveal coordinated fraud, so one operator cannot gain cheaply by minting thousands of identities. Creating more accounts means tying up more capital, while detected Sybils lose that stake; a reef of dormant profiles, a sonnet of plausible messages, or a gale of new sign-ups cannot bypass the bond requirement.
